quiz.question: According to the lesson, what are the three main benefits of using Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)?

answers.answer: It makes your code run faster, use less memory, and require fewer variables.
It automatically fixes bugs, writes comments for you, and chooses the best variable types.
It helps make your code more organized, reusable, and maintainable.
It's the only way to use loops, functions, and conditional statements in Dart.

quiz.question: Imagine you are building an application to manage a library. How would OOP help you organize your code?

answers.answer: By creating one very long `main` function that handles everything related to the library.
By creating classes like `Book`, `Author`, and `LibraryMember` to group related properties and functions.
By storing all the library data in a single `List` of `String`s.
By using `if/else` statements to separate the logic for books and authors.

quiz.question: You have created a `Car` class in your program. If you need to represent 50 different cars, what is the most significant advantage of using this class?

answers.answer: You can create 50 different `Car` objects from the single `Car` class without rewriting the code for each one.
The program will automatically prevent you from creating more than one car.
You must create 50 separate functions, one for each car.
The `Car` class will make your program run exactly 50 times faster.
